s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monoarticular joint pain and swelling with a large effusion in an elderly patient with multiple comorbidities
salient_findings: Right knee pain and increased back pain
5 × 10 cm soft, fluctuant, non-tender mass in the posterior aspect of the right knee
Moderate to large joint effusion without definite synovial thickening
key_facts: History of lung cancer with bone metastases

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute monoarticular joint pain and swelling with a large effusion in an elderly patient with multiple comorbidities
salient_findings: Right knee pain and increased back pain
5 × 10 cm soft, fluctuant, non-tender mass in the posterior aspect of the right knee
Moderate to large joint effusion without definite synovial thickening
key_facts: History of lung cancer with bone metastases

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a large joint effusion and a history of recent aspiration, with laboratory studies showing an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, which is concerning for infection.

shortlist.label: Brucellar arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of treated brucellosis, and the current presentation could be a reactivation or a complication of the previous infection.

shortlist.label: Pseudogout
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of osteoarthritis and presents with a large joint effusion, which is consistent with pseudogout, a type of crystal arthropathy.

shortlist.label: Gout
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of dyslipidemia and presents with acute monoarticular joint pain and swelling, which is consistent with gout.

shortlist.label: Hemarthrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of lung cancer with bone metastases, which increases the risk of bleeding into the joint, especially given the large effusion.

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of lung cancer with bone metastases and is on anticoagulation (implied by the history of transient ischemic attack and atrial fibrillation not explicitly mentioned but common in this population), and the presence of a large joint effusion without synovial thickening or significant laboratory evidence of infection makes hemarthrosis a likely diagnosis

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: The patient is afebrile, has a low white-cell count, and lacks other signs of infection such as erythema or warmth

rejected.label: Brucellar arthritis
rejected.why: The patient was treated for brucellosis 5 years earlier and there is no current evidence of active infection

rejected.label: Pseudogout
rejected.why: There is no mention of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystals in the joint fluid

rejected.label: Gout
rejected.why: There is no mention of urate crystals in the joint fluid
